title: Integral coefficient tensor natural isomorphisms descend uniquely to rational stages
statement: Let $D$ be a finite-field datum, $c$ its coefficient datum with prime $\ell\ne p$, $T_0$ a separated finite-type scheme over $k_0$, and $T$ its geometric fibre [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $E$ be a finite coefficient field in $c.\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Assume $T$ is noetherian, its topological Krull dimension is bounded by a natural number, and $\ell$ is a unit in every local ring. Let $S$ be a finite-stage coefficient comparison [def-fd-coefficient-comparison-datum], with integral functor $J$ and rational functor $H$. Write $U$ and $U_{\mathbf Q}$ for the framework integral completed and rational tensor bifunctors [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Let $R$ be a normalized rational tensor comparison [def-sf-projection-weil-tensor-comparison], with integral ordinary tensor $V$ and rational ordinary tensor $R_{\rm ord}$. Let $q$ and $Q$ denote the recorded source and target integral-to-rational localization functors. For every natural isomorphism $\mu:J\circ U\simeq V\circ(J\times J)$, there is a unique natural isomorphism $d:H\circ U_{\mathbf Q}\simeq R_{\rm ord}\circ(H\times H)$ such that for every pair of integral objects $M,N$, the component $d_{qM,qN}$ is, after the prescribed endpoint identifications, exactly $Q(\mu_{M,N})$.

source.place: Field-stage transport and compatibility with scalar extension; the integral-to-rational comparison elaborated in def-sf-projection-tensor-coefficient-comparison, final proof step

proof.text: Write J and H for the integral and rational functors of the recorded finite-stage coefficient comparison S, and q and Q for source and target localization. S.objects identifies H(q(M)) with Q(J(M)); S.tensors with coefficient 1 identifies their morphism actions. Functor heterogeneous extensionality gives q followed by H = J followed by Q.

The object and bilinear pure-tensor specification of rationalDerivedTensor, evaluated at coefficients (1,1), identifies its restriction along q times q with integral tensor followed by q. The first equality of R.Normalized identifies the corresponding target tensor restriction. Reassociate these equalities to identify the restrictions of both proposed rational bifunctors with the two integral bifunctors followed by Q.

At each unchanged integral pair, transport Q applied to the component of the given integral natural isomorphism mu along the endpoint equalities from the preceding steps. These are isomorphisms and retain their prescribed component maps as heterogeneous equalities. The localization of mu is natural; transporting the two endpoint functor equalities proves naturality of these components on integral arrows.

Source q is a categorical localization by the raw scalar-localization comparison with categorical rationalization. Its product is a localization, and precomposition with this product is fully faithful. Take the preimage isomorphism of the integral natural isomorphism from the preceding step. Its preimage equation gives the required component normalization. Finally every object of the raw rational category is literally an unchanged integral object. Two normalized natural isomorphisms therefore have equal component homs; natural-transformation and isomorphism extensionality prove uniqueness.

lean.statement:
theorem rationalTensorDescent
    (R : WfTensorCompletion.RationalComparison D C T₀ E₀)
    (hR : R.Normalized D C T₀ E₀)
    (mu :
      (letI := sfWeilPrimeInvertible D C.l C.different T₀
       constructibleIntegralTensor C.l (pbcFiniteField C.l C.Qbar E₀)
         (D.geometricFiber T₀).left) ⋙ S.integral.functor ≅
      (S.integral.functor.prod S.integral.functor) ⋙
        WfTensorCompletion.ordinary D C T₀ E₀) :
    ∃! d :
      (letI := sfWeilPrimeInvertible D C.l C.different T₀
       rationalDerivedTensor C.l (pbcFiniteField C.l C.Qbar E₀)
         (D.geometricFiber T₀).left) ⋙ S.rational.functor ≅
        (S.rational.functor.prod S.rational.functor) ⋙ R.ordinary,
      ∀ M N : sfIntegralConstructibleCategory C.l (pbcFiniteField C.l C.Qbar E₀)
          (D.geometricFiber T₀).left,
        HEq (d.hom.app
          ((sfRationalConstructibleLocalization C.l (pbcFiniteField C.l C.Qbar E₀)
              (D.geometricFiber T₀).left).obj M,
            (sfRationalConstructibleLocalization C.l (pbcFiniteField C.l C.Qbar E₀)
              (D.geometricFiber T₀).left).obj N))
          ((pbcStageLocalization C.l C.Qbar (D.geometricFiber T₀).left E₀).map
            (mu.hom.app (M, N)))
